Indiranagar, about four o’clock. Somebody is making filter coffee.The Bengaluru office, where the open roles sit. Pune has people too.

You’ll know everyone here by Friday.

There’s no layer between you and the people who decide things. That’s the best part of the job, and sometimes the hardest.

  1. You’ll be in a client conversation early.

    Intern or delivery partner, you’ll be in the room while it matters, with someone senior beside you.

  2. We argue about hiring decisions in the open.

    At least once a week, usually with the whole company in earshot. If you dislike being disagreed with in front of people, this will be uncomfortable.

  3. The work is learned side by side.

    Reading people is learned by sitting next to someone who is good at it. That’s why the roles are onsite, and why we say so now instead of at offer stage.

  4. Nobody here scores well on everything.

    The founders included. We’re scored on the same six skills and know our own weak ones. It’s the whole argument for writing a bar down.

\ How we hire

The same process we sell.

If we ran a worse process for ourselves than the one clients pay for, you’d be right to notice.

  1. Within 3 days

    A reply, either way

    Including a no, with a reason. We complain about silence in public, so we don’t get to do it here.

  2. 45 minutes

    One conversation

    With someone who has done the job you’re applying for. The questions come from your CV.

  3. Same week

    Your scores, shared

    Against the scorecard above, with your weakest skill named. You get it whether or not we make an offer.

  4. Two weeks, typically

    A decision

    One panel round, then an answer. No take-home that eats your weekend, and no fifth interview to break a tie.

Interns get the same process. Three of the seven roles are entry level or internships, and they get the same conversation and the same written feedback. The people with the least leverage in hiring are usually treated worst.

\ Not seeing your fit
